questions.question: What is the main difference between FileReader and FileInputStream?
options: FileReader reads characters, FileInputStream reads bytes
FileReader is from java.nio, FileInputStream from java.io
There is no difference, both are interchangeable
explanations: Speed depends on the context, not on the class itself.
Correct. FileReader works with characters (it inherits from Reader), while FileInputStream works with raw bytes (it inherits from InputStream).
Both classes belong to java.io.
They are different: one reads text and the other reads bytes.

questions.question: How do you read the entire content of a file as a String in Java 11+?
explanations: FileInputStream cannot be directly converted to a String using the String constructor.
Correct. Files.readString(Path) is a method of java.nio.file.Files available since Java 11 that reads the whole file as a String.
readAll() does not exist in BufferedReader.
File does not have a static read() method that returns content.

questions.question: What is NIO (java.nio) in Java?
options: A newer, more modern and efficient I/O API than java.io
explanations: NIO has no direct relationship with databases.
Correct. java.nio (New I/O) offers a more modern and efficient API with support for buffers, channels, and the file system.
NIO does include networking (channels), but its main purpose is file and buffer I/O.
NIO is not a cache system, but an input/output API.

questions.question: How can you list all the files in a directory in Java?
explanations: readDir() is not a method of the File class.
Correct. file.listFiles() returns an array of File, and Files.list() returns a Stream<Path> with the directory entries.
Directory is not a standard class in the Java API for this purpose.
listAll() does not exist in the File class.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of using try-with-resources for files?
options: It allows reading the file faster
The BufferedReader closes automatically when leaving the block
It prevents any exception from being thrown
It creates a backup copy of the file
explanations: try-with-resources does not affect reading speed.
Correct. try-with-resources declares the resource at the opening and takes care of closing it automatically, even if an exception occurs.
It does not prevent exceptions; it simply manages the safe closing of resources.
It does not create backup copies; it only manages the resource's lifecycle.
